historical_claims.anchor: Many insect-eating bats navigate and hunt using echolocation.
Donald Griffin and colleagues investigated bat orientation and ultrasonic vocalizations in the twentieth century

historical_claims.anchor: Karl von Frisch trained bees with food rewards and tested their responses among cards of different grays and colors.
In a classic style of experiment described by von Frisch, changing the orientation of a polarizing filter altered the direction indicated by dancing honeybees.
In a 2014 study, Hanne Thoen and collaborators found that the animals did not show the fine wavelength discrimination
Subsequent reviews emphasize that the complete mechanism and ecological uses remain incompletely understood.

description: Uses bat echolocation, bee navigation, mantis shrimp vision, and shark electroreception to show how behavioral experiments reveal animal senses without establishing subjective experience.
